title: Quasi-coherent cohomology of Hom from a finite free complex
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $U$ an open subset. Work in sheaves of $\mathcal O_X|_U$-modules on the localized open site over $U$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $E,I$ be cochain complexes indexed by $\mathbf Z$. Suppose there are integers $a,b$ such that $E^i=0$ whenever $i<a$ or $b<i$, and that for every $i$ there is a finite rank $r_i\geq0$ and an isomorphism $E^i\cong(\mathcal O_X|_U)^{\oplus r_i}$. Suppose every cohomology sheaf $H^j(I)$ is quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent]. Then for every integer $n$, the cohomology sheaf $H^n(\mathcal Hom^\bullet(E,I))$ of the ordinary sheaf Hom complex [def-pur-hom-complex] is quasi-coherent. There is no boundedness assumption on $I$.

source.place: Tag 0A6H (2), finite-column calculation; cohomology.tex Tag 08I5, Hom double-complex calculation. Read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0A6H and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08I5.

proof.text: Filter E by successive stupid truncations between its lower and upper bounds. The inclusions have single-term finite-free quotients and split in every degree. Precomposition in the Hom-complex bifunctor therefore gives short exact sequences of Hom complexes. The differential formula in def-pur-hom-complex makes these maps chain maps. This is a finite induction; terms outside the finite interval are zero.

For a source concentrated in one degree with finite free term O^r, the Hom complex is a shift of r copies of I. Finite-free internal Hom is naturally a finite direct sum and is exact; its cohomology is the corresponding finite direct sum of H^j(I). Finite sums of quasi-coherent sheaves are quasi-coherent. This includes r=0.

Use the long exact cohomology sequence of each degreewise split short exact sequence of Hom complexes. For a short exact sequence A -> B -> C of Hom complexes, the long exact sequence gives 0 -> coker(delta^(n-1)) -> H^n(B) -> ker(delta^n) -> 0, where delta^(n-1): H^(n-1)(C) -> H^n(A) and delta^n: H^n(C) -> H^(n+1)(A) are the connecting maps. Thus the cokernel is the subobject and the kernel is the quotient. Kernel, cokernel and extension closure of quasi-coherent sheaves proves the induction step. Transport through the exact equivalence between the localized sheaf-of-modules site over U and sheaves of modules on U.toScheme; quasi-coherence is preserved in both directions since presentations correspond. The induction ends after the finite number of source degrees, regardless of target bounds.

proof_origin.place: Explication of the finite-source case of Tag 0A6H (2) by the finite-column Hom calculation of Tag 08I5.

lean.statement:
theorem finiteFree_homComplex_qc_cohomology
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (U : X.Opens)
    (E I : CochainComplex
      (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U)) ℤ)
    (hEbounded : ∃ a b : ℤ, ∀ i : ℤ, i < a ∨ b < i → IsZero (E.X i))
    (hEfree : ∀ i : ℤ, ∃ r : ℕ, Nonempty (E.X i ≅ SheafOfModules.free
      (R := (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U) (ULift.{u} (Fin r))))
    (hI : ∀ i : ℤ, (I.homology i).IsQuasicoherent) (n : ℤ) :
    ((homComplex (R := X.toRingedSpace.sheaf.over U) E I).homology n).IsQuasicoherent
